FINDING_ID: VC_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.67  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: `load_json()` and the CLI JSON parsers use Python’s default `json.load/json.loads`, which silently accept duplicate object keys with last-wins semantics. In a security-sensitive persistence format, that makes the on-disk artifact textually ambiguous: a reviewer or a different parser can read one value while this verifier actually validates another. The same ambiguity applies to proof files and CLI `--payload` / `--metadata`. The verified object is therefore not the literal JSON artifact, but Python’s lossy parse of it.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Parse chain files, proof files, payload, and metadata with an `object_pairs_hook` that rejects duplicate keys recursively. Fail closed on duplicates and document the format as duplicate-key-free canonical JSON only.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: VC_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.71  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52  
DESCRIPTION: The shipped CLI cannot actually use the advertised Ed25519 authentication feature. `_cli_record()` always creates or loads `VerificationChain` without a `Signer`, so every CLI-created record is `"claimed_only"`. `_cli_verify_chain()` and `_cli_verify_record()` expose no public-key input and always verify with `verifier=None`. So the official operational interface cannot create authenticated records or verify authenticated chains at all, despite the module presenting signing as an available capability.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add CLI options to load a signing key for `record` and a public key or keyring for `verify-chain` / `verify-record`. If that is intentionally out of scope, document the CLI as unsigned-only instead of implying end-to-end auth support.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: VC_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: The programmatic verification API cannot enforce an authentication policy. Even when a `Verifier` is supplied, `_verify_single()` checks signatures only when `signature.attribution == "authenticated"` and silently treats `"claimed_only"` records as successful. A caller therefore cannot ask “is this chain fully authenticated under this key or policy?” and may still receive `All N records verified.` for a mixed or entirely unsigned chain. This is distinct from signature tampering: even honest data cannot be audited under a strict authentication requirement through the current API.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add a strict mode such as `verify_chain(verifier=..., require_authenticated=True, expected_key_id=...)`, or accept a policy/keyring object and fail if any record is unsigned, downgraded, or signed under an unexpected key.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: VC_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.46  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.28  
DESCRIPTION: `verify_inclusion_proof()` is not total over malformed input despite presenting a boolean API. `_digest_bytes()` assumes a string and calls `.startswith()`. If `proof["chain_hash"]` or the supplied `merkle_root` is a non-string value, `_digest_bytes()` raises `AttributeError`, which `verify_inclusion_proof()` does not catch. `_cli_verify_proof()` has the same hole. Malformed proofs should return `False` or exit nonzero, not crash the verifier.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make `_digest_bytes()` validate `isinstance(digest_str, str)` and raise `ValueError` for any wrong type or malformed digest; then normalize all proof-parse failures into `False` in the API and exit code `1` in the CLI.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
